name: Frequency
kicker: Physics quantity · How many repeats happen every second
briefing: Frequency counts how many times something repeats every second, from the vibrations in a guitar string to the oscillations of a light wave, and it is measured in hertz. It is the mathematical reciprocal of a wave’s period, so a higher frequency always means a shorter period between repeats. A photon’s energy depends directly on its frequency, which is why gamma rays carry far more punch than radio waves.

trap.title: Not period, not wavelength
trap.body: This quantity and the period are flip sides of the very same wave: multiply one by the other and the answer is exactly 1, so a question that gives the period and asks what it is the reciprocal of wants this quantity, not the period itself. Wavelength is a different, related quantity entirely, a distance rather than a rate, even though multiplying it by this quantity gives a wave’s speed.
trap.fix: Listen for “reciprocal of the period” or “per second” — that phrasing points to this quantity. If the clue instead measures a distance between wave crests, the answer is wavelength, not this quantity.
